creator: nate.b.jones
title: Plain-English explainer of how agent logins (ChatGPT Work, Grok bot) work via OAuth-style access tokens so the agent never sees your password; hotel-key-card analogy

tools.name: ChatGPT Work (agent login feature)
tools.detail: new feature: sign in to a site in a browser pane, agent acts as you via an expiring access token

tools.name: Grok bot
tools.detail: did the same login-to-token pattern 'a couple of weeks' earlier

tools.name: MCP
tools.detail: cited as the analogy: a pattern that became ubiquitous for agents

claims: ChatGPT Work can sign in to a website with your password but the agent never sees the password
Mechanism: you authenticate directly in the browser to the target site (Amazon etc.); the agent is then issued an access token that lets it act as you on that one site
Access tokens expire, so you periodically have to re-login
Grok bot shipped this first, a couple of weeks before ChatGPT Work
Creator expects this to become a universal agent pattern 'like MCP'
Creator uses it but will not let an agent log in to his bank account
how_to_steps: Open the agent's login screen for the site you want it to use
Enter your credentials directly in that browser pane (goes to the site, not the agent)
The agent receives a scoped, time-limited access token and acts as you on that site
When the token expires, log in again
Decide per-site what you are comfortable delegating (he excludes banking)
on_screen_only: Title card: 'AI Explained: Agent Logins Are Actually Secure. Here's Why.'
Talking head only; no UI, URLs or repos shown
cta: Share with someone who doesn't understand; comment where you would/wouldn't let an agent log in

relevance.why: Useful mental model for explaining agent auth to customers/users of Haji's apps, but nothing actionable for a Claude Code builder; it is consumer-facing explainer content.

implement_score.why: Nothing to implement. At most, when building agent features into an app, use delegated OAuth tokens rather than storing user passwords, which is already standard practice.

verify: Does 'ChatGPT Work' actually use OAuth/delegated tokens vs. a stored browser session cookie (he conflates the two)?
Token scoping claim: a site session cookie is often full-account access, not 'one room' as the key-card analogy suggests

gap.what: Liked set covers app-side security checklists and Jev/agent products, but not a consumer-level explanation of how agents get delegated site access via expiring tokens. Marginal value.
